info.name: BioLM Public
info.description:
[BioLM.ai](https://biolm.ai/ui/home/) offers secure, scalable, GPU-backed APIs to speed up inference, generation, and large language modeling with DNA and proteins. Finetune your own models, or use one of our hosted APIs to the most reputable published models for immediate inference or generation results, in areas like cheap and scalable protein folding, antibody generation, function prediction. We also create and host in-house models where we see opportunity for biotech AI delivered over API, in areas like off-the-shelf biosecurity screening, or fast metagenomic sequence classification via LLM NLP.

Don't forget to install our [Python client / SDK](https://docs.biolm.ai) for easy access. We also have [Jupyter notebooks](https://jupyter.biolm.ai) that demonstrate functional code, and which you can run with your API token.

Visit [BioLM API Tokens](https://biolm.ai/console/user/?tab=api-keys) in your BioLM.ai account to obtain your API Key to use with any of the endpoints in this collection. For each endpoint, you can copy code for making requests in the language of _your choice_ by changing the settings at the top of this page.

To quickly get started making requests with this Collection and Postman, click the _Run in Postman_ button at the top of this page. Then set the `Current value` of the the Postman [Environment](https://learning.postman.com/docs/sending-requests/managing-environments/) variable `BIOLMAI_TOKEN` to your generated BioLM token. This will allow you to immediately use any endpoint you find here.

---

> 🧪 **Mock APIs — NEW!**  
Spend $0 on compute during development with our mock API server.  
Use `mock.biolm.ai` for free dev requests; switch to `biolm.ai` for production.

item.description:
When sending `requests` from in-browser Jupyter notebooks, a pre-flight CORS check is issued to the `https://mock.biolm.ai/api/v3/xxxxx/xxxx/` endpoint. This is an `OPTIONS` HTTP request. In order for the mock server to return a response for these `OPTIONS` requests, we need to have some Postman Examples with the correct CORS headers to pass the pre-flight check.

This needs to include:

- `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` : \*
    
- `Access-Control-Allow-Methods`: `POST, OPTIONS`
    
- `Access-Control-Allow-Headers`: `Authoriziation, Content-Type, Host`
    

You can largely ignore the items in this folder. This simply enables responses when developing with BioLM Mock API in browsers, such as with JS or AJAX.
